title: NANNY | SHORT FILM | Higgsfield Global Film Festival #higgsfieldai
description:
"NANNY" FILM BY LILIT MOVSISYAN FOR  Higgsfield Global Film Festival

Synopsis
Between her mother's two jobs, a girl grows up in a cinema seat, the only place her mother trusts to leave her while she takes a nap.
The place that quietly ends up raising her. Years pass, and somewhere along the way, she stops just watching.

NANNY: a story about love that shows up in unexpected places, made entirely inside Higgsfield. 

#higgsfieldai #HiggsfieldGlobalFilmFestival #higgsfield 



Director's Statement

I'm Lilit Movsisyan, an award-winning filmmaker from Armenia. For most of my career, I envied painters, they could simply take a canvas into their own studio and create, without waiting on financing, without the enormous logistics a film usually demands.

With Higgsfield, that gap has closed for me. I finally have a studio of my own, one where a story like NANNY doesn't have to wait for a budget to exist. 

NANNY isn't just about a mother and daughter going to cinema, it's about every mother who gave everything she had, in circumstances she didn't choose, so her child could have something more. This film is my way of saying thank you, to her, and to every mother like her.

title: UNTITLED US: An Unexpected Connection 🏆 LGBT Drama Short Film
description:
LGBTQI+ Drama Short Film. During a snowy Chinese Spring Festival, a chance encounter between a postman Aiden and Jerome, a man with a traditional Chinese background, leads to a heartfelt conversation that results in a newfound understanding between the two.

Whether it's Queer Drama, Documentary, Horror, Sci-Fi or Comedy, Cannes, Berlin, Sundance or first time filmmakers: Short Frame is home to the best short films from the world’s most innovative filmmaking talent.
-
UNTITLED US is directed by Thomas Mai and published with the permission of the filmmakers. It screened at festivals including Festival du Nouveau Cinéma, Vancouver Asian Film Festival and Lift off Toronto Film Festival.

DIRECTOR'S BIO: Thomas Mai is a Chinese filmmaker and cinematographer based in Vancouver, BC. A graduate of Emily Carr University of Art + Design, he has worked across narrative films, commercials, period pieces, and music videos. His work is driven by a passion for visual storytelling and a desire to explore filmmaking across cultures, with the goal of working internationally as a cinematographer.

title: Auntie Issues | Award-Winning LGBTQ Short Film
description:
🔔 Subscribe for more award-winning films! @ShortFilmBox 

Lola and Veronica are psychology students, and their conversations tend to get a little therapeutic. One day, after a philosophy class like any other, Veronica, who is in love with their teacher and vents about it to Lola, has a revelation: she likes older women because she was in love with her aunt when she was a child!

Writer & Director: Rita Hostt and Tadeo Pestaña Caro
Country: Argentina
Key Cast: Rita Hostt, Nuria Wassaf, Coni Marino, and Ale Granado
Genre: Romantic Comedy
Runtime: 14 min.
Production year: 2023
Original Language: Spanish

Subtitled: English, French, Japanese, Korean, Turkish, Arabic, Vietnamese, Indonesian, Russian, Portuguese, Romanian, Italian, Polish.

Watch more short films here: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLCKIpEHArOA0tXlagax31LfGIDIKIXf1_

Director's Statement: "Auntie Issues is a project born from the need to tell different stories. As a community, we are shaped by prejudices against people who feel and think outside the norm — but there are a lot of us “weirdos”! This project aims to contribute to the visibility of the bisexual community, which remains marginalized even within the LGBTQI+ collective, as well as to the practice of self-managed creation. It’s a very personal story, a sort of self-portrait in which, hopefully, many other people will also see themselves reflected." - Rita
